name: Street Custom 'Judas Cradle' Electrified Knuckle Frame
description: A set of articulated steel knuckle guards wired to a concealed capacitor pack worn at the wrist, delivering a high-voltage discharge on impact. The design originated in bare-knuckle fighting circuits in Tier 1 where augmented fighters needed an equalizer against opponents with reinforced skeletal systems. The discharge is enough to override pain suppression firmware in most commercial-grade cyberware, forcing augmented opponents to feel every hit. Build quality varies wildly — some are precision-machined, others are scrap metal and electrical tape.
specifications:
discharge voltage: 800-2,000V depending on build
capacitor recharge: 3-5 seconds between strikes
weight: 0.3-0.6 kg per hand
power source: Wrist-mounted lithium capacitor, 40-60 strikes per charge
construction: Ranges from machined titanium to salvage steel
story_hooks: A fighting circuit promoter has started requiring Judas Cradles for all competitors — the resulting injuries are drawing attention from people who profit from the fighters staying healthy.
A new variant is circulating that delivers a data-injection payload along with the shock — it's not just hurting people, it's hacking their cyberware on contact.

physical_description.visual_profile: A predatory set of articulated steel knuckle guards with a brutalist, almost skeletal appearance. The guards wrap around the knuckles with sharp, angular protrusions designed to concentrate impact. Thin electrical conduits snake from each knuckle joint down toward the wrist, converging into a compact cylindrical capacitor pack. The overall silhouette suggests organized violence—clinical yet street-born.
physical_description.dimensions: Knuckle frame: 8cm wide × 7cm deep × 4cm tall per hand. Wrist capacitor pack: 12cm long × 5cm diameter. Electrical conduit runs roughly 20cm from knuckles to wrist pack.
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively balanced despite the hardware. The knuckle guards feel substantial and weighted (0.3-0.6kg per hand), anchoring the fist naturally. The wrist pack adds slight rotational pull but distributes evenly. Overall: hefty but not fatiguing for extended wear.
physical_description.primary_material: Machined steel or salvaged titanium alloy (precision builds). Street versions use whatever steel salvage is available—pot metal, automotive scrap, rebar offcuts. Electrical conduits are copper-core with polymer sheathing. Capacitor housing is anodized aluminum or industrial plastic.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal or worn brushed steel with heat-stress discoloration around joint articulations. High-end versions show micro-machining marks and a clean anodized sheen. Street builds: pitted, rust-spotted, electrical tape and solder-drip repair marks. Some feature scorched polymer from capacitor arcing.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray and charcoal black primary, with copper-orange electrical conduit visible beneath translucent sheathing. Capacitor housing often retains industrial warning striping (yellow/black or red bands). LEDs on the pack glow faint blue or red indicating charge status.
physical_description.grip_texture: Bare machined steel knuckles with subtle grip knurling. The contact points where fist meets guard are left raw for maximum contact conductivity. Wrist strap uses reinforced tactical webbing or wrapped electrical tape for insulation. Some street versions wrap in cordwrap or leather for added grip.
distinctive_features: Articulated knuckle segments that flex independently with hand movement
Visible electrical conduit tracing from each knuckle to wrist pack like mechanical tendons
Micro-arc burn marks around joint articulations where electrical stress accumulates
Wrist capacitor pack with exposed cooling fins (small aluminum radiator teeth)
Small LED indicator light (blue/red) on wrist pack showing charge status
Contact pads at knuckle tips—polished steel discs slightly raised for conductivity
Solder joints and flux residue visible on street builds
Optional custom engravings: gang tags, serial scratches, warning labels ('HIGH VOLTAGE')
Heat venting grates on capacitor housing to prevent thermal failure
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Street Custom logo (rough serif 'SC' stamp) typically appears on the wrist capacitor housing, though many street builds have this filed or sanded off. Serial numbering when present is acid-etched into the capacitor shroud. High-end versions feature precision laser-etched warnings. Black-market builds often carry no markings—deliberate anonymity.
physical_description.condition_typical: Varies by tier. Corpo-tier builds: immaculate, regularly serviced, polished steel with minimal wear. Working-class: functional but well-used, minor scoring and discoloration from repeated strikes, occasional solder repair. Ungoverned sector: heavy patina, makeshift repairs, tape-wrapped conduits, singe marks from capacitor arcing, rust bloom on salvage steel. All versions show contact-point wear from impact.
